content:textarea:6:94.name: Paragraph
content:textarea:6:94.html: RICHMOND, VA – When we first came the people told us that the devil had a strong hold here. Now they are led to admit that “Jesus Christ the Lord of all is mightier than he.” During last week some of the devil’s best friends and advocates have farewelled from his kingdom, and declared plainly that now they seek a better life. Backsliders are coming to Father’s house. Christians are working shoulder to shoulder with The Army, and there is joy in the presence of God. We closed the week with four souls in the fountain and Christians drawing nearer to God. We mean Richmond for Jesus.

content:textarea:116:23.html: 2003 – Major Bobby Lancaster is assigned to Richmond as Area Commander, replacing Lt. Colonel Morrow. The Salvation Army Richmond Area Command opens the Cold Night Shelter in which anyone who may be homeless is provided a place to sleep on nights where the temperature is forecasted to be 35 degrees or below. During the first year of the program, the Cold Night Shelter was open for 96 nights and provided refuge for 2,882 people.

Robert Winston, a youth from The Salvation Army Boys & Girls Club, wins the Youth of the Year award in Virginia.

content:textarea:118:86.name: Paragraph
content:textarea:118:86.html: 2005 – The Salvation Army celebrates 120 years of service in Central Virginia with a celebration dinner at The Salvation Army Boys & Girls Club. After Hurricane Katrina hits the Gulf Coast, Richmond Area Command’s Emergency Disaster Services Unit and its 3 canteens are dispatched to assist those in need in Louisiana. All told, Richmond Area Command personnel spend 7 weeks in the Gulf Coast providing aid to those in need and serve more than 28,000 meals. Richmond Area Command serves 236 evacuees who come to Central Virginia looking for assistance.

content:textarea:122:17.name: Paragraph
content:textarea:122:17.html: 2007 – The Salvation Army School of Performing Arts is launched in three locations; the Richmond Citadel Center for Worship and Service, The Salvation Army Boys & Girls Club, and the Petersburg Center for Worship and Service. This school offers free lessons to Central Virginia children, including keyboard, guitar, percussion, woodwind and brass. Other elements of the performing arts include gospel choir, mime, sacred dance and drama for different age groups. The Church Hill Outpost opens at The Salvation Army Boys & Girls Club, offering Christian programming for people of all ages. The Salvation Army, in partnership with ESPN Radio 950 AM and afternoon host Greg Burton, kick off the first annual “Holiday Cheer & Gear” program. This program provides new sporting goods to children in Central Virginia through The Salvation Army Christmas Assistance Programs.

content:textarea:123:37.name: Paragraph
content:textarea:123:37.html: 2008 – Volunteers and officers from Richmond Area Command are activated during The Salvation Army’s national response to hurricanes Gustav and Ike. These individuals provided meals to weary residents along the Gulf Coasts of Mississippi and Texas. In late fall, Richmond Area Command launches Register to Ring, a website that allows individuals and groups to sign up for a time, date, and location to ring a bell at one of The Salvation Army Kettle sites in Central Virginia.

content:textarea:124:50.name: Paragraph
content:textarea:124:50.html: 2009 – The Salvation Army Boys & Girls Club, in partnership with The Salvation Army Women’s Auxiliary, launches a new program; “My Story.” This program aims to teach youth from the Club reading comprehension, writing and spelling, as they write their own biographies. In May, The Salvation Army Adult Rehabilitation Center opens its newest Family Store at 11000 Midlothian Turnpike. Captain David Worthy is assigned to Richmond Area Command, replacing Major Dan Proctor.

content:textarea:141:95.name: Paragraph
content:textarea:141:95.html: 2020  – The Salvation Army Central Virginia Area Command receives approval to relocate from 2 West Grace St. to 1900 Chamberlayne Avenue. During the COVID-19 pandemic, The Salvation Army Boys & Girls club serves as the “R Street Shelter”, providing housing, meals, and health screenings for homeless individuals at higher risk of exposure to coronavirus. The Salvation Army Adult Rehabilitation Center and Family Thrift Stores in the Greater Richmond  Area are consolidated. Captains Jason and Bethany Burns replace Majors Donald and Laura Dohmann as Area Commanders, respectively.

content:textarea:143:27.name: Paragraph
content:textarea:143:27.html: 2023 – A big year of new opportunities and partnerships allowed The Salvation Army Central Virginia to expand its reach and capacity to keep Doing The Most Good:
content:textarea:143:27.content: 2023 – A big year of new opportunities and partnerships allowed The Salvation Army Central Virginia to expand its reach and capacity to keep Doing The Most Good:

content:wysiwyg_basic:144:55.name: WYSIWYG
content:wysiwyg_basic:144:55.html:
• Spring 2023:
    • Harold Harris, a dedicated member of the Richmond Community and The Salvation Army Boys & Girls Club, is honored for Doing The Most Good with the youth in the Richmond Community for more than 40 years, and is recognized for his efforts with an honorary street sign. The block of R street in front of The Salvation Army Boys & Girls Club is officially named Harold Harris Street. 
    • The Salvation Army of Central Virginia launches the first Leaders Doing The Most Good Awards Luncheon recognizing non-profit, corporate and individual excellence in Doing The Most Good in RVA. The Shield Award honorees were Richmond Christmas Mother Fund (non-profit), Ukrop's Homestyle Foods (corporate) and Ms. Mary Ann Wilson (individual).
       
  • Summer 2023: 
    • Majors Samuel and Christine Kim replace Majors Jason and Bethany Burns as Area Commanders, respectively. Fall 2023: The Salvation Army Boys & Girls Club launches the Run for Hope (cancelled due to tropical storm Ophelia), an annual fundraiser to benefit our youth and Club in Central Virginia.
       
  • Winter 2023:
    • The Richmond Christmas Mother Fund celebrates an 89-year partnership with Angel Tree, and Ms. Jacquelin Ukrop Aronson is named the 2023 Richmond Christmas Mother. Thanks to a generous community of donors and volunteers, 4,231 Angels and Silver Bells were adopted and experienced Christmas morning.
    • In a historic private-public partnership, The Salvation Army Central Virginia with the City of Richmond, opens a 150-bed Inclement Weather Shelter from December 1, 2023 to April 15, 2024, at 1900 Chamberlayne Avenue.

content:wysiwyg_basic:147:76.name: WYSIWYG
content:wysiwyg_basic:147:76.html:
• Winter 2024: 
    • On February 12, Richmond City Council made a historic decision to invest in The Salvation Army Central Virginia’s Center of Hope, a $7M city match investment that will address the growing unhoused population and expand shelter services and capacity at 1900 Chamberlayne Avenue, which is currently serving as the season’s 150-bed Inclement Weather Shelter. The three-pronged approach will be: adding more beds for families and single men; providing an on-premise community resource center with wrap-around services for job readiness, financial education and mental health support; and transforming the current building to serve both inclement weather guests and year-round emergency shelter residents.
       
  • Spring 2024:
    • The Salvation Army of Central Virginia hosts the second annual Leaders Doing The Most Good Awards Luncheon recognizing non-profit (Feed More), corporate (Puritan Cleaners) and individual (Reginald "Reggie" Gordon) excellence in Doing The Most Good in RVA. See 2024 DTMG Awards Event Recap
       
  • Summer 2024: 
    • 1900 Chamberlayne expands emergency men's shelter capacity at 1900 Chamberlayne by 50 beds. 
    • 1900 Chamberlayne Inclement Weather Shelter continues to operate it's heat and extreme weather relief shelter as needed.
    • The Salvation Army Boys & Girls Club of Richmond hosts the first in-person Run for Hope at Byrd Park, with 135 runners participating in the 1-mile Fun Run and/or timed 5K. See 2024 Run for Hope Event Recap
       
  • Fall 2024:
    • The City's Community Resource and Training Center opens at 1900 Chamberlayne Avenue to provide support and wrap-around services to clients.
       
  • Christmas 2024:
    • The Richmond Christmas Mother Fund celebrates an 90-year partnership with Angel Tree, and Dr. Lydia Johnson is named the 2024 Richmond Christmas Mother. Thanks to a generous community of donors and volunteers, 4,665 Angels and Silver Bells were adopted and experienced Christmas morning. See 2024 Christmas Recap Reels from Family Day and Kettle Kick Off to the Ribbon Cutting and Christmas Concert.

content:textarea:152:80.name: Paragraph
content:textarea:152:80.html: The Salvation Army has a rich history of service to families and individuals in need in the Central Virginia area. In fact, we’ve been providing service to the area for more than 125 years, thanks to the generous support of local donors, volunteers, and partners who help us live out our Vision of being a focused service provider and advocate for people seeking a path to self-sufficiency in Central Virginia.
